sentences.text: Client Aisha Rahman attended the meeting with the solicitor Daniel Okafor. The purpose was for the solicitor to obtain the client's story and dates straight before providing advice
The meeting took place on Wednesday, 23 September.
Client Aisha Rahman works for Northgate Logistics Limited, described as a big warehouse off the ring road with blue cladding.
Client Aisha Rahman started working at Northgate Logistics on 5 March 2018.
Client Aisha Rahman started as a picker on the floor doing general picking.
Client Aisha Rahman became a team leader for the inbound goods team in June 2021.
Client Aisha Rahman's team consisted of eleven people on her shift.
Client Aisha Rahman works full time on a four on four off rota from 7:00 to 7:00 (approximately 7:15 with handover).
Client Aisha Rahman's basic salary was £29,400 per year; she stated her total including shift allowance and overtime was £31,000.
Client Aisha Rahman received an unsocial hours supplement of approximately £1,800 per year.
Client Aisha Rahman is unsure of her pension contribution rate, estimating it to be either 4% or 5%.
Client Aisha Rahman has Type 1 diabetes since she was fourteen years old.
Client Aisha Rahman manages her Type 1 diabetes using a glucose sensor on her arm connected to a phone app and requires injections.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that she cannot schedule her diabetes management as it depends on workload, heat, and food intake.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that she told her manager, Linda Chu, about her diabetes when she started, and Linda was supportive.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that Linda Chu left at the end of last year to work at a supermarket on the distribution side.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that she and Linda Chu remain friends on Facebook and she still has Linda's number.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that the arrangement for her to step off for five minutes to manage her diabetes was informal, occurring maybe once or twice a shift, and was not in a
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that Linda Chu was her manager until the end of 2025.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that she was team leader of the quarter in 2023.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that Gary Whitlock started as her manager in January 2025 (specifically the 12th of January).
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that Gary Whitlock was initially fine, but was very focused on numbers such as unload rates and dock-to-stock times.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that on 2 February, Gary Whitlock sent an email stating that everyone must take breaks at fixed times (30 minutes and two 15-minute breaks) and no one
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that she went to see Gary Whitlock the same week the new break policy was sent and explained her diabetes needs; he advised her to time her steps off
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed that she was cut off from the work email system the day she was dismissed.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed she has diabetes and requires short breaks to test blood sugar and eat, citing a reasonable adjustment in an Occupational Health report dated 22 April
Client Aisha Rahman stated she emailed HR in March requesting an occupational health referral
Client Aisha Rahman stated the occupational health report was dated 22 April
Client Aisha Rahman stated the report indicated she should be allowed short breaks to test and eat as a reasonable adjustment
Client Aisha Rahman stated she had a phone appointment with a nurse regarding the referral
Client Aisha Rahman stated she believes the occupational health report is in her personal email, which she described as a 'mess' containing school emails
Client Aisha Rahman stated she would find the occupational health report that evening
Client Aisha Rahman stated that nothing changed immediately after the occupational health report was received
Client Aisha Rahman stated Gary (her line manager) said he would 'take it on board' the occupational health report
Client Aisha Rahman stated Gary held an informal conversation with her on 19 May (Tuesday) regarding her team leaving the dock
Client Aisha Rahman stated Gary told her she needed to 'set an example as a team leader' during the 19 May conversation
Client Aisha Rahman stated the 19 May meeting was informal and no warning letter or verbal warning was issued
Client Aisha Rahman stated she had not received any written or verbal warnings in eight years of employment
Client Aisha Rahman stated she had never been late and claimed she opens up half the time
Client Aisha Rahman stated no one had actually told her she was late, though she acknowledged they might have said it
Client Aisha Rahman stated she stepped off the dock on 1 July and 3 July, each time for approximately ten to twelve minutes, and asked Tomasz Nowak to cover
Client Aisha Rahman identified Tomasz Nowak as a team member and unofficial deputy who had been there nearly as long as her
Client Aisha Rahman stated Gary told her 'that's twice this week' in front of everyone on 3 July when she returned
Client Aisha Rahman stated the weather was 30 degrees Celsius on 9 July, describing the dock as an 'oven' with open doors
Client Aisha Rahman stated she was unable to read the scanner on 9 July because she was shaking and going low
Client Aisha Rahman stated she sat down on a pallet on 9 July and Marcus Bell (a first aider) provided her with Lucozade and stayed with her
Client Aisha Rahman stated Marcus Bell took a photo of her blood sugar reading of 2.1 on her phone
Client Aisha Rahman stated she lost consciousness but did not remember all of it
Client Aisha Rahman stated she felt okay after approximately twenty minutes and went to the canteen to eat
Client Aisha Rahman stated Gary told her to go home because she had left the dock without a team leader and claimed she was 'not fit to be here'
Client Aisha Rahman stated she lost approximately four and a half hours of pay on 9 July
Client Aisha Rahman stated Marcus Bell filled in the first aid log
Client Aisha Rahman stated she did not know if Gary filled in any accident forms
Client Aisha Rahman stated she was called to an investigation meeting on 17 July with Dean Farrow (a shift manager)
Client Aisha Rahman stated Dean Farrow asked her about the three days (1 July, 3 July, and 9 July) regarding why she left the dock
The client stated the disciplinary meeting lasted forty minutes or less.
The client reported that the manager did not look at the client during the meeting but looked at his screen.
The client stated they did not receive notes from the disciplinary meeting or from Kerry.
The client initially thought the termination letter was dated the 15th of August but corrected this to the 14th of August after reviewing it.
The client received the termination letter by email on the 14th of August at approximately 5:00 PM.
The client received a physical copy of the termination letter by post on a Saturday.
The termination letter stated employment would terminate with effect from the 14th of August.
The termination letter dismissed the client for 'misconduct, namely repeated failure to follow reasonable management instructions' and did not cite gross misconduct.
The termination letter stated the client was paid in lieu of notice.
The client received eight weeks' pay in lieu of notice.
The termination letter specified the amount as four thousand five hundred and twenty-three pounds.
The client confirmed the pay in lieu of notice arrived in their bank account with the final pay at the end of August.
The client estimated they had approximately six days of holiday left but were unsure if it was included in their final payslip due to confusing codes.
The client stated the termination letter did not mention their diabetes or an occupational health report.
The client stated they had worked there for eight years.
The termination letter informed the client they could appeal within five working days in writing to HR.
The client appealed the dismissal by emailing HR on the 19th of August, copying Kerry.
The client's grounds for appeal included: the dismissal was due to diabetes; the employer ignored the occupational health report; the hearing was inappropriate because Gary was the
The client's grounds for appeal included: the client had never received a warning, not even one.
The appeal hearing was held on the 2nd of September on Teams with Claire Ashdown (regional manager) as the hearing officer.
The client reported the camera froze during the appeal hearing.
The client reported Claire Ashdown listened and allowed the client to talk during the appeal.
The appeal outcome letter was dated the 16th of September and upheld the dismissal.
The appeal outcome letter addressed the grounds: it stated Gary was the right person because he knew the facts best, and regarding the occupational health report, it stated the HRD
The appeal outcome letter stated the employer offered fixed breaks as an adjustment which the client did not use properly.
During the appeal call, Kerry from HR suggested the client might be able to leave quietly but did not specify an amount or offer.
The client stated no documents, settlement agreements, or forms were sent after the appeal call.
The client confirmed they had not signed any documents.
The client reported that Jodie (a colleague on the other shift) told them she heard Gary call the client a 'liability' during a managers' meeting.
The client stated Jodie did not attend the meeting herself but heard the comment from someone else who would not identify themselves.
Client stated she has one interview scheduled for next Tuesday at Harbour Freight, a parcel company near the airport, for a team leader role.
Client stated the interview role pays approximately £27.
Client stated she is worried about references, specifically that Northgate will say she was dismissed.
Client stated she has applied for Universal Credit and is waiting for a response.
Client stated her husband works as a bus driver.
Client stated there are many red entries on the spreadsheet.
Client disclosed she has not been sleeping and her diabetes levels have been rising since her diabetes nurse told her.
Client stated her diabetes nurse informed her her average blood sugar levels have gone up.
Client stated she has not yet seen her GP about her stress or sleeping issues.
Client stated she saw her diabetes nurse in early September.
Client stated she is struggling to get through on the phone to book a GP appointment.
Client expressed concern about a colleague with epilepsy who works night shifts.
Client stated she does not know if she has legal expenses insurance.
Client stated her husband manages their home insurance with Castleford Mutual.
Client stated she was worried about owing money to the solicitor.
Client Aisha Rahman stated she wanted to know roughly how much money she would receive if the case went well.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor stated it was too early to give a figure and that the amount depends on how quickly the client finds work.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor stated he would provide a range once he had the payslips and the client's job search results.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor stated that an agreed reference through ACAS is something that can often be negotiated as part of a settlement and noted this aligned with what the client (
Client Aisha Rahman stated that an agreed reference would be the main thing she wanted.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor stated that nothing had been issued, there was no claim in the tribunal yet, and nothing had gone to ACAS.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor stated he would not make promises about winning the case.
Client Aisha Rahman stated she preferred knowing there were real questions about how the situation was handled rather than being told she would definitely win.
Client Aisha Rahman disclosed she is currently on the street on Cromwell Road, by the church.
Client Aisha Rahman expressed hope that she would leave without a ticket.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor stated the wardens in the area are ruthless.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor stated the weather forecast predicts rain all week and that the weather is finally going to break at the weekend.
Client Aisha Rahman stated she would be glad for the weather change.
Client Aisha Rahman has the original paper contract from 2018 but does not have a copy of the contract she signed when she became team leader.
Client Aisha Rahman does not have a copy of the email sent by Gary Whitlock on 2 February regarding breaks.
Client Aisha Rahman has a certificate showing she was team leader of the quarter in 2023, which she believes is in a kitchen drawer.
Client stated she has a spreadsheet tracking interviews, created by her eleven-year-old, with green for interviews and red for rejections.
Client Aisha Rahman wants to achieve her objectives in order of priority.
Client stated she will book an appointment with her GP.
Client stated her primary objective is for the employer to acknowledge they were wrong to treat her for being ill and provide a proper reference.
Client stated she would like compensation, but acknowledged it is not the main thing.
Solicitor confirmed the client's order of priority: acknowledgement, a reference, and compensation as secondary.
Solicitor advised the client to keep a record of every application, dates, and outcomes, noting that tribunals may argue the client should have done more to find work (mitigating a
Solicitor advised the client to mention her stress and sleeping difficulties to her GP to get support.
Solicitor stated that a tribunal can make recommendations but its powers in this regard are fairly limited.
Solicitor advised the client to check if she has legal expenses insurance, noting it is often bolted on to home or car insurance.
Solicitor advised the client to check the policy schedule and wording to see if legal expenses cover exists.
Solicitor stated that legal expenses insurers usually require the case to have reasonable prospects and sometimes require the use of their own panel solicitors, though the client's
Solicitor stated he would not discuss fees today and would set out options in writing once the insurance policy is reviewed.
Solicitor stated the meeting was free and no bill would be issued for it.
Solicitor stated that employment tribunal claims have very short and strict time limits.
Solicitor stated that before bringing a claim, the client must go through ACAS early conciliation.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor stated he would send a letter confirming today's advice and funding options by Tuesday, the twenty-ninth, which would set out time limits with the thir
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed the client to email him the OH report, Marcus's photo of the sensor, any unpaid payslips, and the February email by Friday, the twenty-fifth.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed the client to check with Castleford Mutual whether they have legal expenses cover and send the policy schedule and wording by Monday, the twenty-
Client Aisha Rahman stated she would have her husband ring Castleford Mutual, noting her husband is off on Monday.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed the client to write a timeline in their own words covering everything told today with dates by next Friday, the second of October.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed the client to keep the spreadsheet going for every application.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed Trainee Sophie Grant to draft a subject access request to Northgate by Monday.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed Trainee Sophie Grant to email the subject access request to the HR inbox and post it to the registered office.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed the client to ask Marcus if he would be willing to give a statement, advising the client to ask without going into detail and not to approach Tom
Client Aisha Rahman stated she would message Marcus and leave Tomasz alone.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed the client to ask Linda if she would be happy to talk to him at some point.
Client Aisha Rahman stated she would message Linda.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor scheduled a follow-up meeting for Thursday, the eighth of October, at ten o'clock.
Client Aisha Rahman confirmed the meeting time, noting her little one has an assembly on the ninth but agreed the eighth is fine.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor instructed the client to send any correspondence from Northgate to him before replying and not to respond to them directly.
Client Aisha Rahman stated she would not sign anything.
Solicitor Daniel Okafor advised the client that if Northgate asks why they left, they should say it is subject to an ongoing process and they would rather not go into detail.
